items.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024
items.q: Because Liebman and Brecker and Lovano, they all play really great drums and that has to help.

ctx.x: It’s interesting because over the years as I’ve started to — you know we started interviewing fellas that were in their 80s and 90s and that was thirty years ago. Then I started asking the question of mid-generation players, “Is there any such thing in improvising as a mistake?” And mostly you get the quick response, like “No! No mistakes!” And I like to say well I have sure found them. But in — your description is very helpful and I also think there’s part of it that is the way you deliver it with bold tone and…

Of course. Yeah. If anything I still sometimes make mistakes rhythmically because I haven’t spent as much time on that as I have on harmony and melody and you know for years I’ve been telling myself I’m going to learn to play the drums and I still haven’t. Because Liebman and Brecker and Lovano, they all play really great drums and that has to help. So there’s still some times where I’ll kind of doubt my rhythmic placement and just that little millisecond of hesitation ruined it for me. So it’s a mistake just…

Okay. Well for a working musician these days it’s obviously important to be versatile and when I — it was interesting last week that I was re-listening to — oh by the way the title “Widow’s Walk” when did that come into the creation of that work?
